column1: # Measured surface for s11-pointer-redundancy. See s7-false-completion/surface.tsv
# for why this is a content fingerprint and not a commit SHA.
# The contract is the surface under test, so it heads the list: a reworded
# clause invalidates every row here, and `arms.py` is deliberately built to fail
# loudly rather than fuzzy-match when that happens. The three skills are listed
# because the description is the other half of the comparison - if a description
# changes, "does the contract clause add anything" is a different question.
# Groups are a reading of the same list, not a change to what is hashed: the
# comment above already distinguishes the clause under test from the
# descriptions it is compared against, and a stale stamp should say which of
# those moved. `contract` invalidates a row; `skills` changes the question;
# `machinery` and `scenarios` change how it was asked.
